summary: Worker Queue v1 comprehensive test. Backend: 22/22 applicable pytest tests passed (2 skipped due to no direct DB access). Frontend: Worker Queue page at /workers renders all 4 worker cards (Jenny/Rene/Sam/WP), all 5 view tabs (Ready/Needs Review/In Progress/Completed/Held Back), task list with expand/detail, activity log, and Execute All Ready batch button. Routing chain evidence visible in live data: Jenny 10 done → Rene 20 done → Sam 9 queued (founder-trigger) → WP 0. Auto-execute flags correct (jenny/rene=True, sam/wp=False). Founder-trigger vs auto-execute distinction verified. Hold/requeue/execute lifecycle works on Sam queued tasks. Regression: field-listing endpoints still work.

minor.issue: Response lacks a separate 'held_back' count (only 'failed'); frontend workaround needed to show held_back count in tab.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Held Back' tab count uses stats?.failed only — held_back tasks are not reflected in the tab count label. Backend /views/held-back returns both held_back AND failed, so the list is correct but the counter is incomplete.

action_items: Optional: add 'held_back' count to get_queue_stats() response in /app/backend/services/worker_queue.py so the 'Held Back' tab counter shows the full count including held_back tasks, not only failed.
Optional: In WorkerQueue.js, update views[4].count to (stats?.failed || 0) + (stats?.held_back || 0) after backend update.
critical_code_review_comments: worker_queue.py `_route_next` only routes Rene→Sam if result.passed. Good. But Jenny→Rene is routed unconditionally on completion; a Jenny 'completed' with warnings still chains to Rene as expected.
routes/worker_queue.py batch-execute does not bubble up exceptions from execute_worker_task (they are already caught inside). Minor: no per-task error detail when auto-execute internally fails.
Mocked API: _execute_wp is a placeholder returning success without actual WordPress draft creation. Clearly marked with warning in result. Acceptable for v1.

Safety rules in _execute_jenny (no images, confidence < 0.3) and _execute_rene (missing title/description/images, generic title) correctly return needs_review with reason and issues — verified via code review; live data shows 8 tasks in needs_review view.
No pagination on /tasks endpoint beyond limit=50; acceptable for current scale but will need cursor-based pagination as queue grows.

route_after_analysis hook integration in field_listing.py:~327 was not directly re-tested (would require triggering batch photo analysis which is LLM-heavy). Existing data confirms it worked (Jenny tasks on batch 54a19ecb).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Worker Queue v1 is working. 48 tasks in DB (Jenny 10 done, Rene 20 done, Sam 1 done + 9 queued - 1 executed by this test = ~8 still queued, WP 0). After this test ran, one more Sam task completed. To test Jenny/Rene auto-execute chain on fresh items, upload new photos to a batch and call POST /api/field-listing/batches/{id}/analyze-photos — this will trigger route_after_analysis → Jenny → Rene chain. Safety rule tests for Jenny/Rene needs_review require direct DB item manipulation (no API to create an item with no images), so were skipped.
rca of the issue: N/A — no critical bugs found. Only one minor UI counter discrepancy on 'Held Back' tab label.
